text:
maria: Hey team — opened a small follow-up PR to the OptKit migration guide that adds a short example for combining batching + KV-prefetch + a quant profile. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821  
kevin: nice, skimmed — looks compact. did you include the Go SDK variant? we get a lot of questions about prefetch APIs there.
devon: not yet. i left a TODO in the PR for go + python parity. i can add the Go snippet if folks are okay with the wording.
maria: please add Go. try to keep the example < 12 lines so it fits the sidebar.
samir: quick note — the quant profile example uses `q4_0` in the PR but our recommender suggests `q3_k` for short-sequence chat. maybe clarify tradeoffs rather than prescribing a single profile.
kevin: +1 on making it advisory. can we add a 1-sentence callout: "prefer lower-quantization for short sequences to avoid hallucination regressions"?
maria: good call. i'll change the language to "recommended" + add a short table row about seqlen.
devon: i pushed a tiny patch expanding the example to show `Batcher.batch_size=8` and `KV.prefetch=True` in both Py/Go. also added a tiny comment about tail-latency.
leo: seeing CI fail on docs lint: "line-too-long in docs/optkit/migration.md:452" — it points to the Go snippet that has a long import path.
kevin: use an alias import and add a comment to avoid the long line, or wrap the import on two lines.
devon: fixed and force-pushed. snippet now 11 lines.
docs-bot: docs-lint: run: success; mkdocs build: warning: missing-anchor for [kv-prefetch] in optkit.md: note: link will 404 in older versions.
samir: about that anchor — we changed the heading once during the restructure. instead of relying on anchor, add an inline link to the API reference page `/docs/sdk/reference/kv-prefetch` and add a redirect notice for older docs.
maria: done. updated link + added a parenthetical "(redirects from /old-guide/kv)" to help bookmarks.
kevin: one more ask: can we add a tiny CLI snippet showing how to run a local microbatch smoke test? people love runnable examples.
maria: added this block (short):
```
# run a local smoke runner
redwood-optkit run --profile q3_k --batch-size 8 --prefetch kv
```
kevin: perfect.
leo: integration tests passed locally for me. staging preview looks good except the sample code fence language is set to "text" — set it to "python"/"go" so it gets highlighting.
devon: updated fences and added a caption under the code samples: "Python / Go examples showing equivalent behavior."
docs-bot: deploy-preview: success — preview URL: https://deploy-preview-4821--docs.redwood.ai
samir: tiny nit: in the recommendations section, can we add a line about monitoring token-cost delta when changing quant profiles? it's easy to forget cost impact when people swap profiles.
maria: ok added: "Monitor per-route token cost and latency after quant changes; expect small token-decoding CPU differences for q3 vs q4."
kevin: LGTM from me.
devon: LGTM, approving PR.
leo: approved as well — merging after CI green.
docs-bot: CI: running full checks...
docs-bot: CI: green. all checks passed.
maria: merged — thanks everyone! i'll tag the migration ticket and add a short note in the release notes for the week. :tada:
kevin: excellent, thanks for coordinating.
samir: great teamwork.
leo: leaving a quick follow-up task to monitor the feedback thread for any confusion around q3_k vs q4_0.
